title: Perdiz con Coles (Partridge with Cabbage)
description: Prepared with partridge, cabbage, and bacon.

ingredients.name: 1 partridge, cleaned, emptied, singed and trussed
ingredients.sourceText: 1 partridge, cleaned, emptied, singed and trussed

ingredients.name: thin strips of bacon, salted two hours prior in brine reinforced with pepper and a pinch of nutmeg
ingredients.sourceText: thin strips of bacon, salted two hours prior in brine reinforced with pepper and a pinch of nutmeg

ingredients.name: 2 sheets of bacon, one for underneath and one on top
ingredients.sourceText: 2 sheets of bacon, one for underneath and one on top

ingredients.name: half a pound of veal loin, sliced
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of veal loin, sliced

ingredients.name: 2 onions with cloves embedded in them
ingredients.sourceText: 2 onions with cloves embedded in them

ingredients.name: 1 glass of fine white wine from San Sadurni de Noya
ingredients.sourceText: 1 glass of fine white wine from San Sadurni de Noya

ingredients.name: half a pound of mixed bacon, cut into slivers
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of mixed bacon, cut into slivers

ingredients.name: 1 good piece of Catalan butifarra or a half pound of ham
ingredients.sourceText: 1 good piece of Catalan butifarra or a half pound of ham

steps: Clean, empty, singe and truss the partridge, and lard its entire breast with many very thin strips of bacon that have been placed in brine two hours prior, reinforced with pepper and a pinch of nutmeg
Place the partridge in a pot with a perforated removable base, between two broad sheets of bacon, one underneath and one on top, after settling the perforated movable base at the bottom of the vessel

Add half a pound of veal loin in slices, 2 carrots, 2 onions with cloves of spice embedded in their flesh, salt and pepper, a bundle of fine herbs, 1 glass of the finest white wine from San Sadurni de Noya and 1 bowl of clean broth
Separately, blanch cabbage heads by boiling them 2 or 3 minutes in salted boiling water
Drain them well and turn them to air them so they do not retain a drop of water
Place them on top of the partridge in the pot, with half a pound of mixed bacon cut into slivers and a good piece of Catalan butifarra or a half pound of ham
Moisten everything with sufficient clean broth and cook over very low heat for two hours, with the pot well covered with its lid
After this time, take the movable piece of the vessel and remove very slowly and carefully all the contents

Place the partridge on a serving platter and set aside the carrots, pieces of veal, butifarra, ham, etc. on another platter, leaving only the cabbages on the movable piece on a plate to squeeze out their juice well, compressing them with a spatula

Meanwhile, reduce the sauce from the pot by half, and place the cabbages on top of the partridge, wrapping the bird completely, and on top of the cabbages place the butifarra or ham in slices or small even pieces
Make a hash from the veal, bacon, onion if any remains and carrots, on which the partridge will be placed on the platter before garnishing it with the cabbages and butifarra

title: Pescadilla Frita (Fried Whiting)
description: Prepared with whiting, flour, and salt.
steps: Clean the whiting
Coat with flour
For whole whiting: form it into a ring by putting the tail in the mouth and pressing with wet fingers to seal
Heat oil until it begins to smoke with a blue hue over high heat
Fry in plenty of hot oil with enough space for the fish to move freely
Season with salt when plating to serve
Use three to four pounds of oil for half a dozen medium-sized whiting in a large pan

title: Pescadilla á la Milanesa (Breaded Whiting)
description: Prepared with whiting, bread crumbs, and flour.
steps: Flour the whole whiting on the outside, and excessively on the inside
Sprinkle with salt and a pinch of pepper, and soak in a beaten mixture of egg and one spoonful of milk
Wrap in toasted bread crumbs and soak again in the egg, then wrap again in bread crumbs
Let dry a little so the crust takes shape, then fry, allowing more time for cooking than for naturally fried whiting
The whiting should result very firm and rolled up, without the shape of the fish being very marked
Serve as is, or with any of the infinite known sauces, but thick tomato sauce is what best suits the dish

description: Prepared with whiting, breadcrumbs, and flour.

Fry for longer than you would for plain fried whiting

title: Pichones á Escape (Squabs in a Rush)
description: Prepared with squabs, lard, and bacon.

ingredients.name: one or two ladles of clear broth
ingredients.sourceText: one or two ladles of clear broth

steps: Cut four squabs into four pieces each
Sauté the pieces in lard with bacon scraps and small mushrooms the size of walnuts
Turn the squab pieces frequently; they will cook in only a quarter hour over high heat
Once ready, remove the squabs from the pan
In the same fat, brown a good tablespoon of flour until it takes on a dark toasted color, and season with salt and pepper
Moisten with one or two ladles of clear broth
Return the squabs to the sauce to soak well and heat through
Arrange the squabs in a mound on a serving dish, pour the sauce over them, and add the juice of one lemon

title: Pierna de Carnero Adobada y Asada (Marinated and Roasted Leg of Mutton)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, bacon, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: One rather lean leg of mutton
ingredients.sourceText: One rather lean leg of mutton

ingredients.name: Strips of bacon that have been in brine
ingredients.sourceText: Strips of bacon that have been in brine

ingredients.name: Broth from the pot without fat
ingredients.sourceText: Broth from the pot without fat

steps: Choose a rather lean piece
Skin it and lard it with strips of bacon that have been in brine beforehand
Submerge the larded leg of mutton in an escabeche made of vinegar and fat-free pot broth in equal parts, salt, pepper, fine herbs, and chopped shallots with a pair of garlic cloves
Allow the leg of mutton to remain in this broth for three days, completely submerged
At the moment of roasting, remove it, drain it, and clean it with a cloth
Rub the entire surface with fine clarified oil
During cooking, continuously moisten the meat with its own juices and serve with them
Note: Small legs of mutton from Pamplona, the region of Burgos, and Cuenca are best for this preparation

If no spit roaster is available and only coal and coke are used for cooking, roasting can be done in the oven, but it is more difficult as one must exercise exquisite care and constantly turn the leg of mutton while continuously moistening it with its own juices to prevent it from becoming toasted on the outside or burned while remaining raw inside
Use oven trays according to the models on page 186, or better, if the kitchen is well equipped, use the roasting pan described in the Appendix

title: Pierna de Carnero Asada (Roast Leg of Mutton)
description: Prepared with leg of mutton, garlic, and butter.
steps: Allow the leg of mutton to age for two days in summer or three to four days in winter, hanging in a cool pantry or larder
Beat the meat vigorously on both sides with a wooden mallet to tenderize it
Place the leg on a vertical spit roaster as shown on page 197
Begin with a lively fire
If the spit does not have mechanical movement, turn the meat frequently
When presenting the meat to the fire, lightly grease it with very fresh cow butter
Dust the entire surface with ground salt to prepare and draw out the juices
Continuously baste the meat with its own juices
Optionally, embed a garlic clove in the handle of the leg
Once the meat has begun to take color, moderate the fire and continue cooking slowly
Cook until no violet-red color remains in the interior of the meat, and when cut it is neither dry from overcooking nor bloody from undercooking
For a piece of five to six pounds, approximately one and a half hours will suffice
Serve from the spit to the table on a very hot platter with the juices in a separate sauceboat
Adapt a screw handle to the leg of mutton before serving
Decorate the bone or handle with a frilled paper rosette or wrap it elegantly with a tea napkin secured with a ribbon so it can be held with the left hand and carved without fork assistance

description: A pudding made with raisins, beef, and bread.

ingredients.name: half a pound of Malaga raisins
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of Malaga raisins

ingredients.name: half a pound of Corinth raisins

ingredients.name: an equal amount of ground salt

steps: Skin and shred the kidney fat with great care and mince it very finely, as if it were bread crumbs
Mix it with the bread crumb and flour, and dissolve with milk
Beat the three eggs well with the nutmeg, ginger, and cinnamon
Mix with the previous mixture and incorporate the citron, orange peel, angelica, Malaga and Corinth raisins, and the glass of rum with the lemon juice, salt, and sugar
Mix everything well with a spatula until the spatula can stand upright planted in the mixture
Grease an appropriate English mold with butter
Cover it with a thick, coarse cloth soaked in water

title: Polla Cebada Trufada (Fattened Hen with Truffles)
description: Prepared with hen, truffles, and bacon.
steps: Clean and empty the freshly killed bird, carefully removing the main bone of the breastbone without tearing the skin
In a separate pan over high heat, sauté 500 grams of truffles cut into quarters in 250 grams of chopped bacon
Stir the truffles with a spatula and let them cook slowly for half an hour in the bacon fat
Remove from heat and let cool
Fill the interior of the bird with the cooled truffle mixture
Place the stuffed bird in a cold place in a basting pan for 34 hours in summer or 48 hours in winter, without touching it, so the meat becomes well infused with the truffle aroma
Roast in the rotisserie covered with a thin sheet of bacon and wrapped in thick well-greased paper
One hour is sufficient to roast the bird over medium heat
Remove the paper and bacon so it takes on color
Serve very hot, plain or in its own juices, sprinkled with some truffle shavings that were set aside earlier

title: Pollo Asado (Roast Chicken)
description: Prepared with chicken, butter or pork fat, and watercress.

ingredients.name: one chicken, four to five months old
ingredients.sourceText: one chicken, four to five months old

ingredients.name: watercress or other edible green vegetable for garnish
ingredients.sourceText: watercress or other edible green vegetable for garnish

steps: Prepare and arrange the chicken well, threading it onto the spit of the roaster and tying it with string so that it does not swing and the legs remain fixed, making a good figure.
Coat the outside with melted butter or pork fat using a kitchen brush. Before tying and fixing on the spit, place inside it about the size of a walnut of the fat being used.
Sprinkle with ground salt and a pinch of pepper.
Roast over a brisk fire rapidly and with much care, because a well-roasted chicken should not be very browned and should have no part of its meat inside that is not completely white.
Serve the roasted chicken alone, without any juice, over a bed of watercress or other green edible vegetable served raw, but not to serve as garnish to strengthen the plate, but only to adorn it.

title: Pollo del Maestro (Master's Chicken)
description: Prepared with chicken, cognac, and oil.

ingredients.name: one plump chicken with full breasts
ingredients.sourceText: one plump chicken with full breasts

ingredients.name: two small glasses of good cognac
ingredients.sourceText: two small glasses of good cognac

steps: Fill the chicken with oil as if it were a vessel and rinse it, then empty it and let it drain.
Incorporate salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg into the interior.
Finish this interior preparation with a splash of two small glasses of good cognac, of the kind drunk by Barbieri, from Cognac in the Lower Charente, a French department.
Once this is done and the chicken is on the spit, coat it with butter from Isigny and roast it over a brisk fire.

description: Prepared with chicken, onions, and bay leaf.

ingredients.name: one chicken, plucked, cleaned and cut into pieces

ingredients.sourceText: one dozen small onions the size of walnuts

ingredients.sourceText: one small glass of good cognac

steps: Cut and quarter a good chicken into pieces.
In a wide, flat skillet, add enough fine oil to just coat the bottom.
Over high heat, sauté the pieces of chicken with a dozen small onions the size of walnuts, one bay leaf, half a clove of garlic, and salt and pepper to taste.
The onions and chicken pieces must brown very well and evenly in just under half an hour, stirring the skillet constantly without stopping.
After this time, remove the chicken from the skillet with a slotted spoon and set aside on a plate.
Pass the fat and onions from the skillet to a saucepan to brown {{source-6}} until it takes on a chestnut color, stirring it constantly for five minutes.
Moisten with chicken broth or water and add one small glass of good cognac.
Once the sauce is thickened, cook over high heat for another five minutes, stirring always with a spatula.
Remove the saucepan from the heat, incorporate the quartered chicken, cover the saucepan well and serve after ten minutes.
Total time: just under one hour.

ingredients.sourceText: 1 piece of pork knuckle the size of a chocolate ounce

ingredients.name: chickpeas (soaked in cold water and salt 6 hours before)

ingredients.sourceText: 4 potatoes the size of an egg

steps: Six hours before starting, soak the chickpeas in cold water and salt.
Pour {{source-0}} into a 3-liter pot and place over heat.

When the water boils vigorously, add half kilogram of beef chuck, then a veal hand, then a marrow bone, and a piece of pork knuckle the size of a chocolate ounce, adding them gradually and successively so the boiling does not interrupt.
While the water continues to boil vigorously, add the chickpeas and salt.
Cook everything over high heat for half an hour with great violence in an uncovered pot.
Then add a small piece of aged bacon, a bouquet of parsley, 2 bay leaves, 3 or 4 leeks cut and tied in a bundle, an onion with 2 cloves studded in it, 2 or 3 turnips, and 2 or 3 carrots.
Without stopping the boil, taste and adjust seasoning, then fill the pot completely with boiling water.
Skim off about 6 spoonfuls of fat, then color with a bit of burned sugar or caramel.
From this moment, half-cover the pot and adjust so cooking is very slow and continuous for 4 hours.
One hour before serving, add 4 potatoes the size of an egg.
To serve the broth, strain through a colander lined with fine linen cloth.

title: Puchero a la Española (Spanish Stew)
description: Prepared with meat, bones, and chickpeas.

ingredients.name: One piece of meat, larger than needed for usual consumption
ingredients.sourceText: One piece of meat, larger than needed for usual consumption

ingredients.name: Two cuartillos of water per pound of meat
ingredients.sourceText: Two cuartillos of water per pound of meat

ingredients.name: Bones from the meat, preferably shin bones
ingredients.sourceText: Bones from the meat, preferably shin bones

ingredients.name: bacon per pound of meat
ingredients.sourceText: Two ounces of bacon per pound of meat

ingredients.name: One quarter of a veal hand
ingredients.sourceText: One quarter of a veal hand

steps: Take a piece of meat larger than needed for usual consumption, as the larger the piece, the fresher and more solid it will be, and it will save time and fuel
Do not wash the meat so as not to strip it of a large part of its juices
Tie or bind the meat after removing the bones so it maintains a presentable shape
When the water in the pot boils vigorously, introduce the meat suddenly
Use two cuartillos of water per pound of meat
After the meat has cooked for a quarter hour, add the bones that the piece had, and some more, preferably shin bones

Add pre-soaked chickpeas and other vegetables such as carrots, parsnips, turnips, a bundle made with leeks, celery, parsley and two bay leaves, and two large onions in which are embedded respectively half a clove of garlic and two cloves of spice
The proportion of vegetables in the stew, not counting the chickpeas, should be in total weight equal to that of the meat
After the vegetables, add the bacon, two ounces per pound of meat, and one quarter of a veal hand
After two hours of slow boiling that has begun since the meat was added, taste the broth and correct the seasoning made at the start
For the broth to be good, the stew must cook slowly and continuously for six hours
To diminish evaporation as much as possible without damaging the cooking, the pot should not be perfectly covered
When adding water, do so carefully with boiling water
For coloring, burn a little ground sugar in a small pan, and when the caramel has formed, introduce the pan and all into the stew until the sugar detaches

To remove the broth from the pot, with a skimmer and carefully, extract all the solid parts that the vessel contains: meats, vegetables, etc., to proceed afterward with their placement and arrangement on the plates to go to the table

Strain the broth through fine linen placed in the bottom of the strainer, which should be well soaked in cold water so that all the fat it contains stays in the linen, resulting in clean and transparent liquid with this natural clarification

description: Prepared with veal, salt pork, and chickpeas.

ingredients.name: a handful of chickpeas soaked the night before

Add a little salt, two pounds veal from the loin area, a piece of salt pork, a handful of chickpeas soaked from the night before and {{source-3}}
Add a quarter chicken and put to cook, taking care to remove the foam

After it has boiled about one hour, add, well peeled and cleaned, a ripe plantain with its skin, a chorizo, a handful of tender beans, half a cabbage, a piece of squash, an eggplant, a little malanga, a piece of Castilian squash, two turnips, two sweet potatoes, four tomatoes, two shallots, one onion and a piece of island squash
Let everything cook about another hour and take care to remove any foam that rises again

To season it, pound in a mortar with a little salt, two or three garlic cloves, a few grains of cumin and cilantro and two of pepper, and when all is made into a paste, dilute it with broth from the pot and add it to the pot with two threads of crumbled saffron
Let it boil a while and serve

description: Prepared with veal, beef, and salt pork.

ingredients.name: a piece of Veracruz or Chicago salt pork
ingredients.sourceText: a piece of Veracruz or Chicago salt pork

steps: Take a pot containing about two jars of cold water
Add {{source-0}}, {{source-1}} and a piece of salt pork
Put on low fire
Add two more jars of water when the first ones have lost their coldness
Increase the fire to produce foam
Remove the foam as it rises until no more appears

After boiling about eight hours on equal fire, and when it has cooked four hours, add half a cabbage, one lettuce, two or three turnips, equal quantity of carrots, a handful of soaked chickpeas, scraps of a turkey, half a chicken and some roasted lamb bones, a little parsley, three cloves and one roasted onion
Add hot water if needed until the eight hours are completed

title: Puchero Belga (Belgian Stew)
description: Prepared with beef, carrots, and turnips.

ingredients.name: from two to six pounds beef
ingredients.sourceText: from two to six pounds beef

steps: Take from two to six pounds of beef and put in a pot, adding half an azumbre of water per pound, and put on moderate fire, which should be increased little by little in order to extract the foam
Remove the foam as it rises to the surface until none appears

Leave the pot for eight consecutive hours on an equal and moderate fire, and after the first four hours, add three medium carrots, two turnips, four leeks, one parsnip or gallego turnip, all cut in half
Add a bundle of parsley, larger or smaller as proportionate, one roasted onion with two or three cloves stuck in it, sufficient salt, and take care to add hot water as the first evaporates
If to this mixture is added a whole bird, or at least half a chicken, the scraps of a turkey or ribs of roasted lamb, the result is a tasty stew

title: Puchero Común (Common Stew)
description: Prepared with chickpeas, beef or mutton, and ham.

ingredients.name: Beef or mutton, well washed and skinned
ingredients.sourceText: Beef or mutton, well washed and skinned

steps: In a pot proportioned to the food to be cooked, add water and once hot, add the chickpeas and meat well washed and skinned; for each pound of beef or mutton, add half a pound of chickpeas
When it begins to boil, skim it, being careful not to overdo it so as not to deprive the stew of its substance
Two hours later, add some ham, bacon and a small onion
Let it all boil at low heat, seasoning with salt and adding warm water from time to time
If half a hen and turkey offal are added to this mixture, one will achieve with such simple and easy method the best of ordinary stew
The broth serves to soak all stews in which a liquid substance is needed without resorting to water
The vegetables are cooked separately with aged bacon, chorizo or blood sausage

title: Puchero Francés (Pot-au-feu)
description: Prepared with meat, carrots, and turnips.

ingredients.name: good fresh healthy meat
ingredients.sourceText: three pounds good fresh healthy meat

ingredients.name: one roasted onion or a little burned sugar for color
ingredients.sourceText: one roasted onion or a little burned sugar for color

steps: For three pounds of good fresh healthy meat put eight quartillos of cold water and salt, letting it cook little by little and skimming it well
Then add carrots, turnips, small onions, parsley, cloves, one garlic clove and one roasted onion, or a little burned sugar to give color to the broth
After cooking six hours on low fire, the puchero is done, and the broth, after straining, is poured over the soup

steps: Six hours before beginning, soak the chickpeas in cold water and salt
In a pot of three liters capacity, pour {{source-0}}
Place on the fire, and when it boils vigorously, add half a kilogram of beef from the part called morcillo
Add one hand of veal, one shin bone, and one piece of codillo the size of an ounce of chocolate

title: Pure de Guisantes (Pea Puree)
description: Prepared with peas, broth, and egg yolk.
steps: Soak dried peas overnight in cold water as you would chickpeas
Cook over gentle heat in a water boiler
Once cooked, pass through a sieve using a mortar pestle, collecting the paste on a deep platter
In a quick-cooking pot, reheat 60 grams of butter from cows per pound of pea paste
Dust with flour without letting it brown or toast
Moisten with broth and thicken
Incorporate the pea paste and stir vigorously over high heat with a spatula
Add half a quarter-liter of milk and season with salt, pepper, and ground clove
Remove from heat at the first boil
Away from heat, bind the puree with an egg yolk beaten in two spoonfuls of cold milk
Serve in a legume dish as it comes from the pot, or on a round platter shaped like a half orange and surrounded by molded croutons

title: Puré de Cebollas (Onion Purée)
description: Prepared with onions, beef, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: three dozen large onions, the size of eggs
ingredients.sourceText: three dozen large onions, the size of eggs

steps: Peel three dozen large onions and chop them very finely.
Sauté them in a pot over high heat in considerable beef butter, without allowing the butter or onions to brown, and dust with flour until everything sets a little.
Season moderately with salt and pepper and moisten with one ladle of fresh water.
Let cook vigorously for a while, stirring constantly with a spatula, and add half a quarter-liter of milk.
From this point forward, cooking must be very slow and will last about fifteen minutes until the broth reduces by half.
Pass everything through a fine sieve, and set the paste to curdle in a bain-marie in another pot, with two egg yolks dissolved in milk at the moment of serving.
This is a luxury dish that is presented with success at great tables, serving as a complement, though separate, to fried ham or grilled salmon.

title: Puré de Patatas (Potato Purée)
description: Prepared with potatoes, egg yolk, and water.

ingredients.name: Salted water, one quartillo (approximately 1.15 liters) per two liters of potatoes
ingredients.sourceText: Salted water, one quartillo (approximately 1.15 liters) per two liters of potatoes

ingredients.name: Cow's milk, cooked beforehand, up to half a quartillo
ingredients.sourceText: Cow's milk, cooked beforehand, up to half a quartillo

ingredients.name: Two ounces or 60 grams of fresh cow's butter
ingredients.sourceText: Two ounces or 60 grams of fresh cow's butter

steps: Steam potatoes of farinaceous variety
If large, cut into pieces the size of walnuts
Using a purée press with tongs, squeeze the potatoes without great effort, passing the fine paste through the colander attached to the apparatus into a plate below
Put a cooking pot on strong heat with one quartillo of salted water for every two liters of potatoes
Incorporate the reserved potato paste
Without ceasing to stir quickly and vigorously with a boxwood spatula, add cooked cow's milk up to half a quartillo
The purée thickens and reaches its point when it boils with bursting bubbles
Then remove from strong heat and leave at the side of the stove to cook gently for a quarter of an hour, being careful that the dish does not stick
At the moment of serving, remove the pot from the heat and add two ounces or 60 grams of very fresh cow's butter
Stir the paste well, holding the pot by a handle, and bind with one egg yolk beaten in {{source-5}} in which salt and pepper to taste have been added

title: Rabo de Vaca á la Hochepot (Oxtail Hochepot)
description: Prepared with oxtail, carrots, and onions.
steps: Cut the oxtail into as many pieces as it has vertebrae, the same as if it were meat for a boiled dinner
At mid-cooking, add six carrots, two onions with their corresponding cloves, and half a cabbage cut into strips, with good seasoning of salt and pepper

When the oxtail is well cooked, after about six hours, remove it from the pot along with the vegetables, and place them on a platter with the pieces of oxtail in the center and the vegetables around it
Degrease the broth carefully, add meat stock, reduce over high heat, and pour this broth over the dish to serve it

title: Raspadura de Berza (Cabbage Scrape Soup)
description: A soup made with cabbage, pork fat, and ham.

ingredients.name: Two or three tablespoons of pork fat
ingredients.sourceText: Two or three tablespoons of pork fat

ingredients.name: Grated cheese of Gruyere or La Mancha (optional)
ingredients.sourceText: Grated cheese of Gruyere or La Mancha (optional)

steps: Cut the cabbage finely, wash it and drain it perfectly
Put it in a pot with two or three tablespoons of pork fat
Sauté over high heat, stirring constantly with a spatula so the cabbage colors evenly without burning
Transfer the cabbage to another pot with a good piece of ham
Add broth from the stew pot and let it boil until the cabbage is well cooked
Drain the contents of the pot well and separate the broth
Line the bottom of the pot completely with slices of brown or rye bread
Layer with cooked cabbage the thickness of the bread, then bread, then cabbage, and so on until the pot is full, ending with a layer of cabbage
Place the pot back over the fire, adding the separated broth in just enough quantity so everything is soaked without oozing
Toast in the oven or with fire on the pot lid placed over hot coals
Serve in the same pot, saving the ham for another meal or as garnish for another dish

steps: Reheat in butter half a pound of raw chicken breast over moderate heat without allowing it to color; when well cooked, remove from pan and let cool and drain to retain as little fat as possible
In the same pan, cook bread crumbs slowly over low heat with several spoonfuls of pot broth to reduce to thick paste
Separately, cook half a pound of veal breast in much water with salt, pepper and two or three carrots; when cooked, let cool
In a marble mortar, successively crush the chicken breast, bread, and veal in that order, then pass each through a fine sieve
Combine the three purées and mix exactly in the mortar in equal parts, adding a couple of spoonfuls of finely chopped fine herbs
Moisten this filling with concentrated broth and let cook until it acquires good consistency

title: Rellenos para las Aves Asadas (Stuffing for Roasted Poultry)
description: Prepared with sausage, liver, and egg yolks.
steps: Prepare by chopping and mixing the sausage meat with the liver of the bird to be stuffed, in quantity proportioned to the volume of the bird, two egg yolks, thirty or forty roasted chestnuts so they do not fall apart when the whole cooks, the crumb of half a roll soaked in broth from the pot, and the appropriate seasoning of salt and pepper.

When the bird is a large turkey or medium-sized duck, the raw liver can be chopped and mixed with the stuffing, but if the bird is small, the liver should be half-cooked beforehand, because the roasting is not taking place long enough for the liver to cook completely as it should.

This stuffing can be rectified and improved by the following method: half-cook the liver and chop it very finely, then mix it with scrapings of truffles well seasoned with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg.

title: Riñonada de Ternera en Caja (Veal Kidney in a Box)
description: Prepared with veal, ham, and beef.

ingredients.name: lean ham cut into very fine strips
ingredients.sourceText: lean ham cut into very fine strips

steps: Lard the veal kidney with strips of very finely cut lean ham
Separately, cook and sauté in very fresh beef lard, taking care they do not burn, a little finely chopped parsley, six shallots and one portion of mushrooms
Season with salt and pepper and moisten with one glass of Sherry wine
In this juice, sauté the veal kidney for a few minutes, cut open in the shape of an open book as mentioned before
Remove the meat from the pan and also remove the fine herbs and vegetables from the juice, well drained, place them on the meat and close the kidney so it recovers the shape it had before being cut
Let it cool, and when it is well cold, wrap it four or six times in as many sheets of paper, like making a package, and around the edge or thickness of the meat tie it with kitchen twine
Thus prepared, cook the kidney in the previous juice for two hours in a pan over high heat, covered with a dome-shaped lid heavily weighted with fire
At the moment of serving, place the kidney on a platter and with scissors cut in a circle the part of paper that corresponds to the surface, leaving everything else, so the meat is as if inside a box
To cover the twine that holds and presses the paper, wrap it around with another white paper, which is ruffled or molded and secured with a pin
Pour the well-degreased and reduced sauce from the stew over the meat and serve this dish by cutting the meat within its own paper case

title: Riñonada de Ternera á la Española (Veal Kidney Spanish Style)
description: Prepared with veal, pork, and bay leaves.

ingredients.name: two ladles of broth or cold water
ingredients.sourceText: two ladles of broth or cold water

steps: In pork lard and in a braising pan or earthenware casserole, brown the veal kidney and make it take color
The fire must be lively for this operation, which will last ten to twelve minutes
Then cover the pan, after seasoning the meat with salt and pepper and adding two bay leaves

Cook on very low heat for three hours, taking care to turn the meat every half hour, and at the midpoint of cooking moisten the meat with two ladles of broth or cold water, incorporating at the same time a sprig of parsley
Serve as roasted veal Spanish style

description: Prepared with veal, beef tongue, and beef.

ingredients.name: two or three glasses of white wine
ingredients.sourceText: two or three glasses of white wine

steps: Cool a cooked beef tongue prepared as in the spicy sauce formula and cut the thickest part into thin slices
Cut these slices into strips or shreds like bacon for larding
Lard the veal kidney prepared as in the previous formula with these strips and brown it well in beef lard
Separately, brown and color two or three finely cut onions very well in refined oil
Moisten with {{source-5}} and strain through a fine sieve to moisten the veal with this sauce
Add good seasoning of salt and pepper, two or three glasses of white wine according to the volume of the kidney, and let everything cook very slowly for two hours
Pass the onions remaining in the sieve through a fine sieve to convert them into a purée
Cook mushroom trimmings in this purée very slowly so the sauce thickens gradually
Place this garnish on the meat and in the serving dish to complete the plate

title: Rodaballo á la Holandesa (Turbot Dutch-Style)
description: Prepared with turbot, lemon, and beef.

ingredients.name: sea water or very salty water
ingredients.sourceText: sea water or very salty water

steps: Rub the turbot on all sides with two lemon halves before placing it in the water.
Cook the turbot in a turbotera (a diamond-shaped cooking vessel) with short broth, using sea water or, in its absence, very salty water.

The fish is cooked as soon as the water reaches its first boil, and it can be served immediately, or it can remain in the water away from heat for as long as desired without the cooking point being altered.
Remove the turbot from the turbotera and place it on a platter over a well-pressed napkin that serves as a bed for the fish.
Serve melted beef butter that has been warmed in a bain-marie with a pinch of salt in a sauce boat.
When the turbot is served cold, each diner seasons it to taste with oil and vinegar.
Garnish the platter with fresh parsley branches, whether served hot or cold.

Immediately release the dough from the mold
Turn it over and remove it to dust with sugar

title: Rosbif (Roast Beef)
description: Prepared with beef, bay leaves, and shallots.

ingredients.name: A piece of beef, never as large as the English volume
ingredients.sourceText: A piece of beef, never as large as the English volume

steps: Twelve hours before putting it on the spit, place the piece of rosbif in good refined oil seasoned with salt, pepper, chopped parsley, two bay leaves, and some chopped shallots
Turn the rosbif frequently so that it soaks evenly
Roast it for two or three hours, depending on size
Do not remove the meat from the spit until its interior is cooked but maintains a rosy color without releasing blood
Serve at natural temperature with its own juices in a sauce boat, and around the meat may be placed some potatoes in the Dutch style shaped like zucchini, peeled after being cooked in steam

description: Prepared with lamb kidneys, beef, and breadcrumbs.
steps: Remove the membrane from the kidneys
Cut each kidney lengthwise along the outer curved line without completely separating the two halves so they form a single piece when opened
Thread three kidneys onto each skewer, piercing through both halves of each kidney
Soak the prepared kidneys in melted beef butter that has not boiled
Coat with breadcrumbs mixed with salt and pepper
Place the kidneys on live coals on a grill and turn twice to cook through
If using reed skewers or larding needles, remove the kidneys before serving
If using presentable skewers, serve the kidneys still threaded on the skewers, each one being one guest's portion, accompanied by a piece of lemon to eat the kidneys plain

title: Salchichón Casero (Homemade Sausage)
description: Prepared with pork, fat, and grains.

ingredients.name: Half pound of very fat bacon
ingredients.sourceText: Half pound of very fat bacon

steps: Mince together the pork loin and bacon; the mixture need not be very fine
Season with plenty of salt, pepper, grated nutmeg, and a few grains of coriander
Fill beef intestines of variable length with this mixture
Hang the sausage inside the kitchen chimney to cure in smoke for ten days, being careful it does not burn, and wrap it first in three or four sheets of brown paper
During this time, burn a little retama in the chimney three or four times so the sausage comes out exquisite
After smoking, cook the sausage in water with salt, pepper, carrots, onions studded with cloves, and a few bay leaves
Two hours of slow cooking are sufficient to finish the operation
Let the sausage cool in the same water in which it cooked
Remove, let drain, and eat sliced into thin slices, the thinner the more flavorful

Two hours of slow cooking are sufficient to finish the operation
Let the sausage cool in the same water in which it cooked
Remove, let drain, and eat sliced into thin slices, the thinner the more flavorful

description: Prepared with ham, veal tongue or mutton or tongue, and rabbit or hare.

ingredients.name: a piece of veal tongue or two or three pieces of mutton tongue, cooked beforehand
ingredients.sourceText: a piece of veal tongue or two or three pieces of mutton tongue, cooked beforehand

steps: Make a brown sauce moistened with a cup of pot broth and a glass of white wine, reduced to achieve some consistency.

In this sauce, cook good lean ham, a piece of veal tongue or two or three pieces of mutton tongue (cooked beforehand), poultry breasts, leftover rabbit or hare, poultry livers, a handful of mushrooms, and artichoke hearts.
Cut all ingredients into equal size and shape, like dice.
Season well with salt, pepper, nutmeg, and a bouquet of fines herbes.
Cook slowly for half an hour until all is well soaked in the sauce.
Remove the bouquet and decant the sauce into another saucepan.
Give the sauce more consistency with a little potato starch.
Stir vigorously and add the salpicón when the sauce is well thickened, or better, if the salpicón has been kept very hot, place it on a serving dish and pour the sauce over it at that moment.

title: Salsa Bechamel (Béchamel Sauce)
description: A sauce made with broth, meat, and cream.
steps: Reduce over high heat half a liter of glaze to which a couple of ladles of good meat broth from the pot has been incorporated
Let it cook, stirring the liquid constantly until it decreases by one third of its original volume
Separately also reduce by one third half a liter of cream
Mix the cream with the reduced sauce, stirring always until it has the consistency of a clear paste
Then strain by pressing firmly through a clear strainer
If the dish it is destined for is not yet ready, it is necessary to maintain the temperature of the sauce in a water bath so it does not cool

title: Salsa Blanca (White Sauce)
description: A sauce made with beef, egg yolk, and flour.

ingredients.name: two large tablespoons of fine flour
ingredients.sourceText: two large tablespoons of fine flour

ingredients.name: one egg yolk without the germ
ingredients.sourceText: one egg yolk without the germ

steps: In a metal saucepan, add two large tablespoons of fine flour
Gradually, with cold water and a boxwood spatula, knead the mixture away from the fire on the kitchen counter
Once the dough is formed and without stopping stirring, continue adding water to produce a very clear and uniform liquid
Place the saucepan on low heat and continue stirring with the spatula very quickly until the mixture begins to boil
Then remove from the heat and leave in a place where it can continue cooking very slowly for ten minutes without needing further attention
At the moment of serving, remove the saucepan from the heat and add {{source-2}}, salt and a touch of pepper
Stir vigorously to mix everything and activate the melting of the lard, and add the liaison
The liaison is one egg yolk without the germ, dissolved in {{source-6}} in a glass, all this without ceasing the movement with the spatula

title: Salsa de Aceite (Oil Sauce)
description: A sauce made with oil, egg yolks, and salt.
steps: In a pan placed over embers or inside a bowl with boiling water, dissolve 4 egg yolks with salt and pepper
Once these are warm, pour 125 grams of good clarified oil over them and shake the mixture vigorously
Prevent the sauce from cooking and ensure it does not get too hot, as the eggs would separate from the oil, the binding would fail and the sauce would not work
Make it at the precise moment of serving as an accompaniment to vegetables cooked in water
Alternatively, submerge a bowl for a few minutes in boiling water, remove and dry quickly, and while it retains heat, prepare the mixture of eggs with oil and its corresponding seasoning

steps: Mix together in a pan 1 tablespoon of flour with ground salt, white pepper in powder and a pinch of nutmeg

Before serving, strain through a metal mesh strainer

title: Salsa Española (Spanish Sauce)
description: A sauce made with bacon, ham, and veal.

ingredients.name: veal kidney without bone and without fat
ingredients.sourceText: two pounds of veal kidney without bone and without fat

steps: In a saucepan, add the bacon and ham, all cut into small pieces or strips.
Place on top {{source-2}}, and make the meat sweat with some spoonfuls of concentrated broth, cooking slowly until the juices run.
Incorporate some onions and carrots during the cooking.
Prick the meat in different places with the point of a knife so all the juice comes out, then add abundant concentrated broth to cover the contents of the saucepan.
Add fine herbs in a bundle, salt, pepper, and some cloves, and let cook very slowly for about two hours.
Pass the sauce through a sieve and to give it consistency, bind it with flour, making the liaison separately and dark, done skillfully.
Mix the liaison with the sauce, place the saucepan over heat, and reduce by slow cooking to one quarter.

When about to use in a stew, for example, add two spoonfuls of this sauce to a small pan with a glass of white wine, Sherry, or Champagne, let reduce considerably over high heat, and incorporate pieces of truffles and mushrooms.

title: Salsa Mayonesa (Mayonnaise Sauce)
description: A sauce made with egg yolks, white pepper, and vinegar.

ingredients.name: two raw egg yolks without the germ
ingredients.sourceText: two raw egg yolks without the germ

ingredients.name: three to four drops of vinegar

ingredients.name: one and a half tablespoons of refined oil per egg yolk
ingredients.sourceText: one and a half tablespoons of refined oil per egg yolk

steps: In a porcelain bowl, placed inside a bowl filled with fresh water or in a very cold place (because the sauce breaks with the heat developed by manipulation), add two raw egg yolks without the germ.
Season well with salt and white pepper, thinning them with three or four drops of vinegar.

Drop by drop, in the proportion of one and a half tablespoons of very refined oil per egg yolk, incorporate the liquid, stirring constantly with a spatula in circular motions, using a stopper with a hole to dispense the oil very slowly.
Beat vigorously without stopping and at the same pace for a quarter of an hour.

When the oil and eggs have bound together and the sauce has the point of a thin cord and tends to separate from the bowl, flavor it with lemon juice, and if none is at hand, with a little good vinegar.

title: Salsa Mayor (Major Sauce)
description: A sauce made with hen, partridge, and ham.

ingredients.name: well-cured ham, trimmed into very thin slices
ingredients.sourceText: one pound of well-cured ham, trimmed into very thin slices

ingredients.name: half a dozen bird feet, charred beforehand on grills
ingredients.sourceText: half a dozen bird feet, charred beforehand on grills

ingredients.name: one glass of good white wine
ingredients.sourceText: one glass of good white wine

steps: Place the hen, partridge, ham, veal shoulder, charred bird feet, bundle of fine herbs, carrots, and onions in a pot with some spoonfuls of concentrated broth.
Cook all this over low heat, and when the juice has taken on good color, add broth in sufficient quantity to cover everything in the pot.
Let cook for three hours over gentle heat, after skimming and seasoning appropriately.
Pass the boiling juice through a moistened napkin and let cool.
Break two eggs in a terrine, and crushing the shells well, beat them together with the yolks and whites, two spoonfuls of broth, one glass of vinegar, and another glass of good white wine.
Add all this to the cooled and well-degreased major sauce and place the pot over high heat.
Remove the sauce from heat before it begins to boil, cover the pot with a lid upon which good coals are placed, and keep the vessel near the fire.
From time to time, uncover the pot to see how the clarification operation is proceeding, and as soon as it is at the right point, strain again through the moistened napkin.

Reheat at medium fire in a saucepan, flour in beef or pork lard until everything takes on a truly golden color

Without ceasing to stir, once the brown sauce has taken on this color, cover the saucepan hermetically, remove from heat and place some coals on the lid when there is no oven, so that the sauce continues cooking for half an hour without risk of burning from direct fire
From time to time uncover the vessel to stir the sauce
The flour cooked properly, without tasting burned, will give the brown sauce a good color tone and an exquisite flavor
Later moisten with broth, water or as stated previously, without seasoning at all, as this remains for the moment when the brown sauce is incorporated into a dish

title: Sopa Bisque (Bisque Soup)
description: A soup made with crayfish, beef or butter or lard, and flour.

ingredients.name: beef butter or lard (for 1 liter of soup)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 ounce beef butter or lard (for 1 liter of soup)

steps: Cook many crayfish excessively, seasoning well.
Remove the feet and tails, which are set aside on a plate and crush and flatten the bodies or corselets, aiding the operation with a bit of the water in which they cooked.

Give everything a boil and strain through a sieve the pasty broth or purée that results, which will be more concentrated according to whether the quantity of crayfish and water respectively is greater or lesser.
In a pan, place to melt 1 ounce of beef butter—for a liter of soup—or lard, and sauté a spoonful of flour, allowing it to take color.
Moisten with the water of the crayfish until the paste curdles, and then increase in the necessary quantity, adding the crayfish purée.
Allow to cook five minutes on medium heat; bind as has been said and pour it into the tureen, where the cleaned tails and feet will be beforehand.

title: Sopa de Alcalde Mayor (Lord Mayor's Soup)
description: A soup made with celery, onions, and water.

ingredients.name: Fine herbs including parsley, chervil, bay leaf and mint
ingredients.sourceText: Fine herbs including parsley, chervil, bay leaf and mint

steps: Cook four pig ears and four pig hands slowly over low heat in {{source-2}} for four hours
Add a bouquet made with parsley, celery and thyme and some onions with cloves stuck in them
After four hours, remove the ears from the broth, which will be very cooked, and leave the hands to cook for two more hours
Strain the broth through a fine sieve, let cool, and when cold remove all the solidified fat from the surface
Debone the ears and hands and cut the meat into very small pieces, place in a covered dish with a napkin until ready to prepare the soup
In a pan over gentle heat, melt {{source-8}}, to which add, stirring constantly with a spatula, all the flour it can absorb
Keep this mixture over the fire for ten minutes while stirring, taking care that the flour does not brown
Gradually incorporate the prepared broth, letting it cook for a while after each portion is added
When all the broth is in the pan, season and dress the meat from the ears and hands with two tablespoons of fine herbs - parsley, chervil, bay leaf, mint, all chopped like tobacco

Add a bouquet made with parsley, celery and thyme and some onions with cloves stuck in them
After four hours, remove the ears from the broth, which will be very cooked, and leave the hands to cook for two more hours
Strain the broth through a fine sieve, let cool, and when cold remove all the solidified fat from the surface
Debone the ears and hands and cut the meat into very small pieces, place in a covered dish with a napkin until ready to prepare the soup
In a pan over gentle heat, melt 250 grams of butter, to which add, stirring constantly with a spatula, all the flour it can absorb
Keep this mixture over the fire for ten minutes while stirring, taking care that the flour does not brown
Gradually incorporate the prepared broth, letting it cook for a while after each portion is added
When all the broth is in the pan, season and dress the meat from the ears and hands with two tablespoons of fine herbs - parsley, chervil, bay leaf, mint, all chopped like tobacco

title: Sopa de Arroz con Leche de Almendras (Rice Soup with Almond Milk)
description: A soup made with rice, bay leaves, and almonds.
steps: Cook the rice slowly in water with little salt, the lemon zest, and two bay leaves
Prepare almond milk by crushing 250 grams of shelled almonds in a marble mortar, adding one spoonful of water during the crushing to prevent the oil from separating
Place the paste in a white napkin to drain well
Dissolve the paste in one quartillo of slightly warm water, passing it through the napkin by compression five or six times, continuously wetting the napkin with the milk
Sugar the rice and give it the right cooking point by adding the almond milk very slowly while it cooks gently
Remove the lemon zest, bay leaves, and cinnamon if used
Serve the rice flavored with orange flower water

title: Sopa de Caldo Consumado (Consommé Broth Soup)
description: A soup made with beef, vegetables, and hen.

ingredients.name: beef, carefully cleaned of all fat
ingredients.sourceText: One kilogram of beef, carefully cleaned of all fat

ingredients.name: Vegetables and seasoning as used in a good puchero
ingredients.sourceText: Vegetables and seasoning as used in a good puchero

steps: In {{source-0}} with the same vegetables and seasoning as used in a good puchero, cook one kilogram of beef, with the piece carefully cleaned of all fat.
At the same time, over very high heat, half-roast a hen, that is, color and brown it well, without it being cooked inside.
Place the hen in the pot and let it cook until the beef is perfectly cooked.
This operation cannot last less than eight hours. The boiling shall be very slow, but without any interruption, and the broth should reduce by half.

This consommé broth, which is taken plain or which serves as the best broth for all broth-based soups, is easy to make and is not relatively expensive for a household that habitually prepares it. The hen meat, minced, has many applications: for fillings, croquettes, etc.

title: Sopa de Fideos (Noodle Soup)
description: A soup made with noodles, broth, and salt.
steps: Add broken noodles by the handful to boiling broth.
Let them cook without becoming too soft, stirring occasionally with a wooden spoon.
Remove the saucepan from the heat when the noodles begin to dissolve, as this would cloud the soup and diminish its pleasant flavor.
For clear soup, use thirty grams of noodles per liter of broth. For thicker soup, double the amount of noodles.
Serve immediately as this soup is only good when made at the moment of serving.

title: Sopa de Nullas (Noodle Soup)
description: A soup made with egg yolks, broth, and flour.
steps: Combine the fine flour with salt and a pinch of pepper. Incorporate the necessary water to give the dough good consistency, adjusting so that the flour can be absorbed by the yolks without adding water.
Work and knead the dough, then extend it with a rolling pin into thin sheets.
Cut the sheets into long strips about half a centimeter wide or even thinner, or shape the scraps as desired.
Let the nullas rest for a couple of hours exposed to air before using.
Add them to the broth as described for noodles, and they must cook for at least half an hour.
This is a very nutritious soup.

description: A soup made with peas, broth, and beef.

When the vegetables have taken on color and the peas have cooked for half an hour, add the sautéed vegetables to the broth

Remove the peas and reduce them to a puree
Mix the puree with the broth, adjusting the consistency with more or less liquid, or letting it reduce if too thin
Twenty minutes before finishing, cut the white part of a celery stalk into strips, sauté it in beef butter, and cook it in the pea soup for that time

Serve hot

Operate in all ways as is known, and when served place in the soup tureen the reserved tail, cut into small cubes

At the moment of serving, add a bottle of Madeira or Port wine with quenelles cut into slices; but these are not added to the soup until everything is ready.

title: Ternera Asada á las Finas Hierbas (Roasted Veal with Fine Herbs)
description: Prepared with veal, shallots, and beef or pork fat.
steps: Prepare a marinade with lots of parsley and two or three shallots, chopped fine and dissolved in a couple spoonfuls of refined oil, to which salt and pepper are added
Rub the piece of veal successively on all sides with this marinade so that by the time it goes to the roaster it has absorbed all the oil from the marinade
Spread the chopped fine herbs well soaked in oil over the entire surface of the veal
Wrap the meat tightly in greased paper, fastened securely with string to prevent the herbs from shifting or falling
When the roast is nearly cooked and only needs to take on color, carefully remove the paper
Using a metal spatula, collect the fine herbs adhered to the paper and meat

Place these herbs in a pan with 125 grams of beef or pork fat and a spoonful of flour to make a blonde sauce, moistened and extended with a little broth or the degreased juices from the roast and a thread of vinegar
Serve this sauce separately in a sauce boat, and the veal on a platter, garnished with watercress dipped in salted water

title: Tortilla a la Española (Spanish Omelet)
description: Prepared with potatoes, lard or oil, and fat.

ingredients.name: lard or oil in large quantity
ingredients.sourceText: lard or oil in large quantity

steps: Fry the potatoes cut like coins in lard or oil in large quantity.
Before they toast or become crispy, remove them from the pan and set aside on a plate, sprinkling them with a little salt.
Remove excess fat from the pan, leaving three tablespoons, and put the pan back over high heat.

At this moment, the twelve egg whites should be beaten beforehand, separately, until foamy, and the twelve yolks, also well beaten, with two tablespoons of fresh water and the seasoning of salt and pepper that the omelet is to have.
Mix the whites and yolks and beat them together while the pan is on the fire.
When the fat smokes blue, without stopping beating, pour the mixture into the pan and beat it still inside for a few seconds, during which the set-aside potatoes are incorporated.
With the left hand shake the pan in a circle, imprinting it with a circular movement so that the omelet, as soon as it sets, begins to turn on its base, but in the opposite direction.
That is the moment to turn it over to the other side, using a tinplate kitchen utensil if needed.
With this apparatus turn the omelet at will, and proceed in the same way so that it sets on the other side.
As the setting becomes firmer, increase the shaking so that the dish colors equally, according to the operator's preference.
The Spanish omelet should be solid, well-combined, round and of great thickness.

description: Prepared with beef, eggs, and water.

ingredients.name: fresh unsalted beef butter
ingredients.sourceText: two ounces of fresh unsalted beef butter

ingredients.name: fresh beef butter
ingredients.sourceText: one ounce of fresh beef butter

steps: Beat ten to twelve eggs in a bowl with a steel fork with long tines.
Add {{source-1}}, which serves to make the mixture of yolks and whites more intimate.
Season with salt and a small pinch of pepper.
Melt two ounces of very fresh unsalted beef butter over high heat in the pan, and when it is shiny and about to take color, pour in the beaten eggs and stir with a spatula until it begins to set.
Once it sets well and always holding the pan by the handle, lift the omelet on one side with the tip of a kitchen knife, and through the opening pass more beef butter in the amount of one ounce.
Once it has melted, fold the omelet in half over itself, and with the pan tilted mold and straighten the edges or sides, and turn it out onto a serving platter to serve it very hot.

description: Prepared with lemon or orange, eggs, and sugar.

steps: Separate the egg yolks from the whites of six eggs.
Put {{source-1}} into the yolks along with the grated zest of a lemon or orange, or a hint of vanilla—any aroma you wish—and beat it all very quickly.
Beat the whites separately until they form stiff peaks, with nothing else added.
In a silver or metal oval serving dish, melt {{source-4}}.
Place the dish over high heat.
Mix the whites and yolks quickly and pour into the dish.
Cover with a dome cover loaded with considerable heat.
Five minutes, by the clock, are enough for the omelet to puff up.
At that moment sprinkle with sugar, an operation that must be done skillfully between the kitchen and the table so that it is presented puffed up and burning.

title: Tostón al Golpe de Estado (Roasted Suckling Pig)
description: Prepared with suckling pig, bacon, and water.

ingredients.name: One suckling pig, fifteen to twenty days old
ingredients.sourceText: One suckling pig, fifteen to twenty days old

ingredients.name: Small wooden sticks or reeds for supports
ingredients.sourceText: Small wooden sticks or reeds for supports

steps: Select a young suckling pig between fifteen and twenty days of age.
Kill the animal and submerge it completely in a caldron of boiling water.
Once clean and white, split it down the belly, opening it lengthwise from the snout to the tail inclusive.
Empty it entirely and wash it well inside and out, drying it thoroughly with burlap.
Extend it as if it were tanned hide and pierce it lengthwise with the spit of the roaster, using small canes or reeds as crosspieces so that it does not close.
Prepare a simple brine of water and salt.
With a kitchen brush dipped in this brine, coat and moisten it well on all sides.
Place it before a fire of burning wood coals, turning it constantly.
At each turn, rub it with a piece of good bacon rind, then moisten it again with the brine, until the skin forms blisters and acquires a hazelnut color.
One and a half hours should suffice for the operation.
The bacon rind is preferable to butter because butter softens what is toasting, while bacon makes it crisp and friable.

title: Turtle Soup (English Style) (Sopa Inglesa)
description: Prepared with beef, carrots, and onion.

ingredients.name: 1 kilo of lean veal with little bone
ingredients.sourceText: 1 kilo of lean veal with little bone

ingredients.name: half a calf's head, well deboned, without brains and without tongue
ingredients.sourceText: half a calf's head, well deboned, without brains and without tongue

ingredients.name: 3 coffee spoons of finely chopped parsley
ingredients.sourceText: 3 coffee spoons of finely chopped parsley

ingredients.name: 2 dozen quenelles of meat or poultry breast
ingredients.sourceText: 2 dozen quenelles of meat or poultry breast

steps: In a pot or marmite with {{source-0}}, add 2 kilos of beef sirloin, 2 or 3 carrots, 1 onion, 1 celery stalk, 1 bunch of fine herbs, {{source-6}} and {{source-7}}.

When the meat is well cooked, strain the broth, let it cool and put it back on the fire with 1 kilo of lean veal with very little bone. Let it cook slowly until the meat separates from the bone, being careful that the boiling does not accelerate so that the broth does not reduce too much.
Separately, have ready half a calf's head, well deboned, without brains and without tongue. These should have been cooked beforehand to reinforce the substance of the soup with their broth.

Pass the first broth through a hair sieve, letting the meat drain well. Let it cool to remove the solidified fat. Then wrap the half calf's head like a cloth, securing it with twine, and place this package and the tongue loose in a marmite, pouring the first cold broth over it and letting it cook over low heat for three quarters of an hour, or at most one hour.
Place the half calf's head and the tongue in a deep baking dish, pour the broth over it and let it cool. This precaution is so that the calf's head does not take on color.
On the other hand, cut {{source-10}} into very thin slices, which are then subdivided into small square pieces, and mince 4 shallots.
In a 4-liter pot, melt {{source-12}}; add the ham with the shallots, half a dozen cloves, a little nutmeg, 1 sprig of thyme, 3 coffee spoons of finely chopped parsley, and half a lemon in slices.
Keep this mixture on the fire for one hour, being careful that the butter does not blacken and constantly sautéing the contents of the pot.
Then add {{source-18}} gradually, and after cooking this for a few minutes, pour the defatted broth free of the sediment that forms at the bottom of the baking dish in small portions.

Keep everything on the fire, but without cooking, for four hours, and after that time strain the broth through a sieve, passing it to another vessel. Cut the calf's head and tongue into fine and equal pieces, and as if they were slices of bread, add them to the broth.

For this soup to be more delicate, cut the skin and fatty parts of the calf's head into thin leaves; when the soup is for a family meal, without guests, cut the meat of the head and glutinous parts at the same time, but it is preferable to set aside the lean meat, even if the soup remains clearer.

With everything prepared this way, put the soup in a baking dish and let it cook for one hour, so that the calf's head is tender. Add a touch of Cayenne pepper and a little salt if the seasoning does not seem very spiced.
Three minutes before serving, add the juice of 1 lemon, 2 glasses of Sherry and 2 dozen quenelles of meat or poultry breast to the turtle soup.

title: Té (Tea)
description: Prepared with tea and water.
steps: Heat the teapot by pouring boiling water into it, then empty it
Put in as many heaping teaspoons of tea as there are cups desired
Pour a small quantity of boiling water over the leaves
Let it rest for three or four minutes, covering the teapot well
Pour boiling water in the necessary amount
Serve the tea
More tea can be obtained by adding boiling water again, but never reuse leaves that have already released their aroma this way

steps: After cleaning the chicken, divide it into pieces by cutting at the joints and season lightly with salt
In a skillet or pot, heat butter until very hot, then add a little garlic, half an onion and parsley, being careful to fry all this without burning
Once this is well fried, add the chicken, turning it so it takes color
Immediately add water until it covers the chicken, and when the chicken is half cooked, add potatoes in pieces
When the potatoes are well cooked the tínola is ready
This dish should be broth-like
The potatoes can be replaced with calabash or zucchini according to taste

title: Vaca Cocida en Pepitoria (Boiled Beef in Pepitoria Sauce)
description: A sauce made with beef, onions, and beef or pork or lard or oil.

ingredients.name: Sixty grams of beef or pork lard, or oil
ingredients.sourceText: Sixty grams of beef or pork lard, or oil

ingredients.name: A couple of ladles of broth
ingredients.sourceText: A couple of ladles of broth

steps: Finely chop parsley and onions.
Sauté them in sixty grams of beef or pork lard, or oil if preferred, being careful that the fat does not brown.

steps: In a pot of adequate capacity, place the piece of beef shaped like a brick.
Pour {{source-1}} and brown the meat well.
Add three pounds of trimmed onions, a quarter pound of bacon in loose pieces, a hand of veal, salt and seasoning, parsley and other herbs in a bouquet, carrots, turnips, and parsnips if available.
The water released by the onion is all the liquid the stew should have.
When the onion softens and begins to paste, add one quarter of a unit of red wine and half of vinegar.
Cook everything over high heat for one hour until the broth reduces by half, then three more hours consecutively over very low heat with the pot hermetically sealed.
Serve this piece of meat as a first course with the vegetables around it and the hand of veal in small pieces alternating with them, all moistened with the little broth or liquid that remains.
Leftovers, kept whole for the next morning breakfast, can be served cold with fried eggs, breadcrumbs, salad, or as desired, and make an excellent second course.

Leave the tarragon branches in the bottle, replenishing the vinegar as it is used so that it remains saturated with the aroma of the plant.

description: Prepared with thrush and bacon.

ingredients.sourceText: thin sheets of bacon, very thin

steps: Pluck and clean the thrush very well.
Open them not to remove the innards, but only the crop or gizzard.
Make a hole below one leg, press the bird, and the crop will come out on its own.
Wrap with thin sheets of bacon, but very thin.
Thread them by half-dozens, inserting a thin spit rod between the wing and the leg, in such a way that the bacon sheets do not come loose.
Fix the rod to the spit so it does not move, and roast at high heat for twenty minutes.

title: Artichoke hearts in tomato-caper sauce
description: Roasted tomato, garlic and onion make a chunky sauce for tender artichoke hearts. Capers and vinegar add briny sharpness, while breadcrumbs lightly thicken the sauce.

ingredients.name: plain frozen artichoke hearts
ingredients.substitution: Use the same drained weight of plain cooked artichoke hearts; avoid marinated hearts because they change acidity and salt.

ingredients.name: ripe tomatoes
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of drained canned peeled tomatoes; texture will be softer.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.substitution: Use the same volume of sunflower or canola oil.

ingredients.name: minced garlic
ingredients.substitution: Use 0.5 g garlic powder per 3 g fresh garlic, added with the liquid rather than fried.

ingredients.name: chopped onion
ingredients.substitution: Use the same weight of white or yellow onion.

steps: Heat the oven to 220°C / 425°F. Halve {{tomato}} and place cut-side up in a small roasting dish. Roast for 20–25 minutes, until softened and lightly browned, then mash.
Simmer {{art}} in a saucepan of water for 8–12 minutes, or according to the package, until a knife enters the base easily. Drain well and halve any large hearts.
Heat {{oil}} in a pan. Soften {{onion}} for 5–7 minutes, then stir in {{garlic}} for 30 seconds. Add the mashed tomatoes, {{capers}}, {{vinegar}}, {{water}}, {{crumbs}}, {{salt}} and {{pepper}}.
Fold in the artichokes and simmer for 8–10 minutes, until the sauce thickens.

description: Tender artichoke hearts are coated with crisp golden breadcrumbs and gently fried garlic. Olive oil gives the crumb topping richness without a sauce.

description: Prepared with artichokes, chicken, and ham.

title: Alcachofas Rellenas (Stuffed Artichokes with Pork)
description: Prepared with artichokes, pork, and ham.
steps: Remove the top leaves from well-cleaned artichokes and cook with salt.
Once cooked, remove and let all water drain completely.
Dry with a cloth.
Have prepared a filling of partially cooked pork, cooked ham in small pieces.

Fry this in one tablespoon of manteca or mantequilla with tomato, onion and peeled and chopped garlic, chopped hard-boiled egg yolks, pepper powder, cinnamon and clove, one teaspoon of saffron water and one teaspoon of bread powder.
Fill the artichokes with this, tie with hemp twine, making sure the filling does not spill out.
Place in a cooking pot with one tablespoon of oil, salt, two bay leaves, some Castilian pepper and ham pieces.
Place in the oven and when serving, remove the spices.

title: Almibar de Cidra (Citron Syrup)
description: Prepared with water, salt, and sugar.

ingredients.name: one and a half pounds of sugar clarified per pound of fruit
ingredients.sourceText: one and a half pounds of sugar clarified per pound of fruit

steps: Peel the cidra and chop into very small cubes imitating hail
Throw into a little boiling water and when it has boiled a few times remove that water and return to the fire with hot clean water
Add one tablespoon of salt
When blanched, remove and place in cloth and tie well under the stream of water for three days
After three days remove and place in clarified honey
When the fruit has heated through add cinnamon strips
Always take care to clarify one and a half pounds of sugar for one pound of fruit

title: Almibar de Durazno (Peach Syrup)
description: Prepared with peaches, cinnamon or fig, and water.
steps: Put some water with a ladle of sifted ash in a vessel, and when it comes to a boil throw in ten peaches
When they peel, remove them and wash in very clean water
Make three cuts with a knife down the middle of each peach
Have one pound of sugar already clarified
Put the peaches in the clarified sugar to heat
They should boil for two hours over moderate heat
When they begin to reach the proper consistency, add cinnamon strips or a fig leaf
Remove when the syrup has reached medium point

title: Almond Cake
description: A cake made with egg whites, egg yolks, and almonds.

ingredients.name: half a pound of ground and peeled almonds
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of ground and peeled almonds

steps: Beat the four egg whites and eight yolks separately
When both are well beaten, combine them
Add half a pound of ground and peeled almonds
Pour into a buttered mold
Place in the oven or in a bain-marie
When cooked, remove and place in a clean mold
Have the clarified sugar at half-thread stage with a glass of sherry
Coat the cake with this mixture and return to the oven

sourceSteps: Wash and grind the pineapple with the meat of one coconut if it is not too acidic
Dissolve everything with the water from the coconut
Have three pounds of sugar clarified beforehand to medium syrup stage
Add the coconut mixture and cook until it reaches the soft-ball stage (punto de ante)
Decorate with raisins and almonds
